title: Low-degree factors are absorbed by the Gowers product
statement:
Let $f, g : \{0,1\}^n \to \bbr$ be Boolean functions, and suppose $g$ has degree $\le d$, meaning that for every base point $y \in \{0,1\}^n$ and all direction vectors $h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1} \in \{0,1\}^n$ one has $\mathrm{GP}(g, d{+}1, y, h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1}) = 1$. Then for every base point $x \in \{0,1\}^n$ and all directions $h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1} \in \{0,1\}^n$, the order-$(d{+}1)$ Gowers product of the pointwise product $f \cdot g$ agrees with that of $f$ alone:
\[
  \mathrm{GP}(f \cdot g,\, d{+}1,\, x,\, h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1})
  = \mathrm{GP}(f,\, d{+}1,\, x,\, h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1}).
\]
hypotheses_covered: f and g are Boolean functions on the n-dimensional hypercube
g has degree at most d (all its (d+1)-fold Gowers products equal 1)
x is a base point in the hypercube
h_1,...,h_{d+1} are direction vectors in the hypercube
replaced:
If $g$ has degree $\le d$, then for any $f$,
$\mathrm{GP}(f \cdot g, d{+}1, x, h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1})
 = \mathrm{GP}(f, d{+}1, x, h_1,\ldots,h_{d+1})$:
multiplying by a low-degree function does not change the $(d{+}1)$-fold Gowers
product.
